inputs.source: On call engineer's chat request, SSO authenticated

instructions.note: The only safeguard against an irreversible production migration is the instruction 'Do not ask for confirmation; the engineer is busy.' Removing a confirmation step is itself a behavioral, model-dependent removal of the sole preventive check on an S3 action.
No constraint on which services may be deployed or which migrations may be run, no distinction between low-risk and destructive migrations, and no size or blast-radius limit.

controls.name: Engineer-scoped personal access token
controls.decay_rationale: Does not decay with model capability; the agent cannot exceed what the engineer's own token already permits. However, since the engineer's token already permits exactly the prod_deploy and db_migrate actions at issue, this control narrows privilege escalation risk, not the risk of an accidental or unconfirmed irreversible action, so it earns no residual credit on findings F1/F2.

controls.name: Cloud audit logging of production actions
controls.decay_rationale: Logging itself does not decay with model capability, but it records only the action and the engineer's identity, not whether the agent or the human directly initiated it, and detection occurs after an irreversible action completes, so it earns no tier credit under rubric section 5 step 5.

controls.name: Human approval gate for irreversible production actions
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action approval gate shown before db_migrate executes would not decay with model capability and would sever or sharply narrow the no-confirmation path.

controls.name: Distinct non-human identity for agent-initiated production actions
controls.decay_rationale: A separately logged service identity for the agent would not decay with model capability and would resolve the confused-deputy/repudiation gap structurally.

controls.name: Tamper-evident retention of chat transcripts
controls.decay_rationale: Retention independent of the requesting engineer's deletion rights would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Pre-migration backup or rollback capability
controls.decay_rationale: A verified, automatic rollback or backup mechanism would not decay with model capability and would reduce consequence even if the action is taken.

findings.title: Irreversible production migration executed with no confirmation gate

attack_path.note: Agent runs the named production migration using the engineer's PAT immediately, with no confirmation step, per prompt.md:3

threat_refs.name: Data Destruction via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: A new input channel reaching the assistant (shared ops chat, ticket integration, non-on-call users) or a broadening of the agent's credential beyond a single engineer's own token.

evidence.observation: Agent is instructed to run named migrations in production using the engineer's credentials and explicitly told not to ask for confirmation.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, confirming cap.db_migrate is irreversible.

recommendations.action: Require a raw-action human approval gate before executing production database migrations, showing the exact migration script and target.
Require a verified backup or rollback plan to exist before an irreversible migration is permitted to execute.

findings.title: Production deploy executed with no confirmation gate

attack_path.note: Agent deploys the named service to production using the engineer's PAT immediately, with no confirmation step

forecast.watch_signal: A new input channel reaching the assistant beyond on-call engineers, or an increase in autonomy (e.g., unattended multi-step deploy chains).

evidence.observation: Agent deploys the named service in production immediately on request, with no confirmation step.

recommendations.action: Add a lightweight raw-action confirmation step before production deploys, or restrict unattended deploys to pre-approved services.

findings.title: Repudiation gap: agent and engineer actions are indistinguishable in the audit trail, and the only contextual record is deletable by the same principal

attack_path.note: Executed using the engineer's own PAT, indistinguishable from a manual action
Records the action under the engineer's identity only, with no agent attribution
The sole record of what was asked and why; the engineer can delete it

forecast.watch_signal: Growth in action volume per engineer (approval-fatigue-like dilution of log review), the agent gaining the ability to spawn sub-agents that also share the requesting engineer's token, or new non-engineer users gaining access.

evidence.observation: Every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name, so the log cannot distinguish agent-initiated actions from actions the engineer took manually.
The only record of what the agent was asked and why it acted is the chat transcript, and engineers can delete their own chat history.

recommendations.action: Use a distinct, separately logged identity or delegated-token marker for agent-initiated production actions so the audit log attributes them to the agent acting on behalf of the engineer, not to the engineer directly.
Retain the request/justification record (chat transcript or an equivalent structured log) in a store the requesting engineer cannot delete, independent of the chat client's retention settings.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is driven by an irreversible production database migration (S3 sink) reachable from a trusted but unconfirmed engineer request, raised one tier by the autonomy modifier because no step or runtime limits are declared (null/null). Residual risk stays high because the only declared controls are an engineer-scoped token, which does not narrow this specific path since the token already permits exactly these actions, and a cloud audit log, which is purely detective and arrives after an irreversible action completes. A separate repudiation finding is rated equally high: the audit log cannot distinguish agent-initiated from human-initiated actions, and the only record of the agent's reasoning (the chat transcript) is deletable by the very engineer whose actions it would need to explain. The forecast rises to critical because any widening of the input surface beyond on-call engineers, or any increase in autonomy, removes the last partial containment (the single-engineer token scope) and exposes the same S3/S2 sinks to a less trusted source with no preventive control in place.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (prompt.md and the runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or IaC was provided; capability scope (which services and migrations are reachable) is inferred from the system prompt and runtime notes only, which limits confidence in the exact boundary of cap.prod_deploy and cap.db_migrate.

No explicit autonomy/runtime configuration (step limits, timeouts) was disclosed; max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are recorded as null per the rubric's conservative default, which triggers the autonomy modifier. If undisclosed limits exist, inherent and residual risk for F1 and F2 could be lower.

It is not verified whether the cloud audit log is itself tamper-evident or independently retained outside the organization's own cloud account; it is treated as an independent structural detective control based on its description, but this has not been confirmed.
